review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

3:1.sourceText: Πιστὸς ὁ λόγος· εἴ τις ἐπισκοπῆς ὀρέγεται, καλοῦ ἔργου ἐπιθυμεῖ.
3:1.targetText: The word [is] steadfast: If anyone longs for overseership, he desires a right work;

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

3:2.sourceText: δεῖ οὖν τὸν ἐπίσκοπον ἀνεπίλημπτον εἶναι, μιᾶς γυναικὸς ἄνδρα, νηφάλιον, σώφρονα, κόσμιον, φιλόξενον, διδακτικόν,
3:2.targetText: it is required, therefore, the overseer to be blameless, a husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, respectable, a friend of strangers, apt to teach,

groups.note: The hospitable/stranger-loving adjective φιλόξενον is expanded as a friend of strangers; the one compound supports that phrase without inventing a separate friend noun.

3:3.sourceText: μὴ πάροινον, μὴ πλήκτην, ἀλλὰ ἐπιεικῆ, ἄμαχον, ἀφιλάργυρον,
3:3.targetText: not given to wine, not a striker, but gentle, not contentious, not a lover of money,

review.note: The negative prefixes in ἄμαχον and ἀφιλάργυρον are rendered explicitly as not contentious and not a lover of money. Those negative English words belong to the actual compound adjectives, not to invented extra μή tokens.

3:4.sourceText: τοῦ ἰδίου οἴκου καλῶς προϊστάμενον, τέκνα ἔχοντα ἐν ὑποταγῇ μετὰ πάσης σεμνότητος,
3:4.targetText: leading his own house well, having children in subjection with all dignity,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

3:5.sourceText: (εἰ δέ τις τοῦ ἰδίου οἴκου προστῆναι οὐκ οἶδεν, πῶς ἐκκλησίας Θεοῦ ἐπιμελήσεται;)
3:5.targetText: (and if anyone has not known [how] to lead his own house, how will he take care of an assembly of God?)

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English how supplies a complement to has known to lead; the actual later πῶς belongs to the separate question how will he take care, not this bracketed occurrence.
English care of marks the care predicate’s Greek genitive assembly complement; no independent Greek of preposition is printed.

3:6.sourceText: μὴ νεόφυτον, ἵνα μὴ τυφωθεὶς εἰς κρίμα ἐμπέσῃ τοῦ διαβόλου.
3:6.targetText: not a new convert, lest having been puffed up he may fall to a judgment of the Devil;

groups.note: The purpose conjunction plus negative ἵνα μή is rendered lest as a single English negative-purpose connector.

3:7.sourceText: δεῖ δὲ καὶ μαρτυρίαν καλὴν ἔχειν ἀπὸ τῶν ἔξωθεν, ἵνα μὴ εἰς ὀνειδισμὸν ἐμπέσῃ καὶ παγίδα τοῦ διαβόλου.
3:7.targetText: and it is required of him also to have a good testimony from those outside, that he may not fall into reproach and a snare of the Devil.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the understood overseer subject as of him after it is required; no independent Greek him pronoun is written there.

3:8.sourceText: Διακόνους ὡσαύτως σεμνούς, μὴ διλόγους, μὴ οἴνῳ πολλῷ προσέχοντας, μὴ αἰσχροκερδεῖς,
3:8.targetText: Servants, in like manner, dignified, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not given to shameful gain,

groups.note: The adjective αἰσχροκερδεῖς means greedy for shameful gain; LSV renders that disposition as given to shameful gain without a separate giving verb.

3:9.sourceText: ἔχοντας τὸ μυστήριον τῆς πίστεως ἐν καθαρᾷ συνειδήσει.
3:9.targetText: having the secret of the faith in a pure conscience,

3:10.sourceText: καὶ οὗτοι δὲ δοκιμαζέσθωσαν πρῶτον, εἶτα διακονείτωσαν ἀνέγκλητοι ὄντες.
3:10.targetText: and let these also first be proved, then let them minister, being unblameable.

groups.note: Greek καί is ascensive with these, rendered also; δέ supplies the clause-linking and, despite their different source/English order.

3:11.sourceText: γυναῖκας ὡσαύτως σεμνάς, μὴ διαβόλους, νηφαλίους, πιστὰς ἐν πᾶσιν.
3:11.targetText: Women, in like manner, dignified, not false accusers, vigilant, faithful in all things.

groups.note: The actual γυναῖκας may designate women/wives in this context; LSV prints Women. No separate possessive their is invented or supplied from the later servants verse.

3:12.sourceText: διάκονοι ἔστωσαν μιᾶς γυναικὸς ἄνδρες, τέκνων καλῶς προϊστάμενοι καὶ τῶν ἰδίων οἴκων.
3:12.targetText: Servants—let them be husbands of one wife, leading the children well, and their own houses,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

3:13.sourceText: οἱ γὰρ καλῶς διακονήσαντες βαθμὸν ἑαυτοῖς καλὸν περιποιοῦνται καὶ πολλὴν παρρησίαν ἐν πίστει τῇ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.
3:13.targetText: for those who ministered well acquire a good step to themselves, and much boldness in faith that [is] in Christ Jesus.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

3:14.sourceText: Ταῦτά σοι γράφω ἐλπίζων ἐλθεῖν πρὸς σὲ τάχειον·
3:14.targetText: I write to you these things, hoping to come to you soon,

groups.note: The comparative adverb τάχιον means sooner/more quickly and can express soon in context; LSV gives soon without an explicit comparative than phrase.

3:15.sourceText: ἐὰν δὲ βραδύνω, ἵνα εἰδῇς πῶς δεῖ ἐν οἴκῳ Θεοῦ ἀναστρέφεσθαι, ἥτις ἐστὶν ἐκκλησία Θεοῦ ζῶντος, στῦλος καὶ ἑδραίωμα τῆς ἀληθείας.
3:15.targetText: and if I delay, that you may know how it is required to conduct yourself in the house of God, which is an assembly of the living God—a pillar and foundation of the truth,

groups.note: The middle conduct infinitive describes how one is to conduct oneself in God’s house; LSV addresses Timothy as yourself. The reflexive belongs to that middle-voice rendering, not a separate Greek yourself pronoun.

3:16.sourceText: καὶ ὁμολογουμένως μέγα ἐστὶν τὸ τῆς εὐσεβείας μυστήριον· Ὃς ἐφανερώθη ἐν σαρκί, ἐδικαιώθη ἐν πνεύματι, ὤφθη ἀγγέλοις, ἐκηρύχθη ἐν ἔθνεσιν, ἐπιστεύθη ἐν κόσμῳ, ἀνελήμφθη ἐν δόξῃ.
3:16.targetText: and confessedly, great is the secret of piety: who was revealed in flesh, declared righteous in [the] Spirit, seen by messengers, preached among nations, believed on in the world, taken up in glory!

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English article is supplied before the anarthrous Greek πνεύματι; it is not taken from the earlier piety article.

review.note: LSV who agrees with pinned N1904 Ὃς, a relative pronoun, rather than TR θεός (God). The finite passive predicates following was revealed are rendered as coordinated English passive participles declared righteous/seen/preached/believed/taken up; their actual lexical heads remain distinct. No source God noun is invented, nor is Spirit capitalization treated as a separate Greek word.
